scenarios.title: Connect to your vault
changes: Make the selected server explicit before entering account information.
Use a compact, centered sign-in form with a clear Continue action and secondary enterprise sign-in.
scenarios.notes: Saved accounts and self-hosted server entry remain supported. Debug demo access is not a production sign-in option.

scenarios.title: Sign in with a master password
changes: Preserve account and server identity across steps.
Keep password entry, reveal, and the sign-in action together; place device sign-in as a secondary route.
scenarios.notes: The form is a sign-in proposal; no password or master key is sent to the review artifact.

scenarios.title: Create an account
changes: Group server and identity separately from the master-password fields.
Explain the password hint briefly and keep field errors next to the affected input.
scenarios.notes: Registration completion and email verification continue to follow the existing server responses and Web Vault continuation.

scenarios.title: Verify two-step login
changes: Name the active verification method and account before the code field.
Keep alternate methods, recovery, and resend actions secondary to verification.
scenarios.notes: The representative screen depicts a code-based challenge. Security keys and Duo use their existing method-specific action without a code field.

scenarios.title: Use a recovery code
changes: State the consequence of recovery before the input: configured two-factor methods are removed.
Keep the return-to-another-method action easy to find and avoid making destructive recovery the default route.
scenarios.notes: Recovery is a separate existing authentication branch with higher consequence than a normal one-time code.

scenarios.title: Unlock your vault
changes: Show the locked account and server while keeping vault contents out of the composition.
Distinguish unlocking from signing out; preserve available Hello, PIN, and enterprise unlock paths.
scenarios.notes: Hello and alternative unlock availability depend on the persisted session and device configuration.

scenarios.title: Approve this device
changes: Make the fingerprint phrase the visual focus of device approval.
Show waiting status, expiration, and cancellation in a stable layout with no sensitive vault data.
scenarios.notes: Other-device approval, administrator approval, and browser SSO remain distinct service-dependent flows.

scenarios.title: Authentication feedback and recovery
changes: Place actionable status near the primary control without shifting the identity header.
Separate retryable authentication failure from local-data cleanup and irreversible reset actions.
scenarios.notes: The visible proposal is a retryable error. Busy controls remain disabled while a request is pending; local deletion and quarantine recovery keep their existing distinct confirmations.

scenarios.title: Vault overview and navigation
changes: Use a calm NavigationView-like rail, a compact command area, and clear list/detail boundaries.
Make search persistent, show active filters, and keep sync status readable without competing with Add item.
Use row selection, focus, and hover as separate states; reserve accent color for the active destination and primary action.
scenarios.notes: Archive mutations and organization actions remain gated by the capabilities and permissions already present in source. Navigation labels are existing destinations.

scenarios.title: Vault with no item selected
changes: Keep a populated list available while the detail pane gives a quiet selection prompt.
Avoid showing credentials until the user has chosen an item.
scenarios.notes: This composition is the initial state after sign-in, unlock, or returning to My vault: a populated vault with no selected item. It is distinct from the selected-login showcase and the empty-account state.

scenarios.title: Login details
changes: Use a stable list/detail layout with one primary Edit action and a quieter overflow menu.
Align field labels, values, reveal controls, and copy controls; retain masking for sensitive values.
Separate frequently used credentials from notes, attachments, custom fields, and history.
scenarios.notes: Synthetic data only. The detail composition reviews representative type-specific fields and common item actions; it is not an exhaustive rendering of every source field or disclosure. Secret reveal and clipboard feedback are separate interaction states.

scenarios.title: Select and organize items
changes: Replace scattered batch commands with one contextual selection bar and an explicit selected count.
Explain unavailable actions for mixed ownership or permissions before submission.
scenarios.notes: Folder moves, ownership transfer, and collection assignment remain separate existing operations; the proposal does not merge their permissions.

scenarios.title: Empty vault onboarding
changes: Give a true empty vault one clear Add item action and a secondary route to existing import.
Keep the empty illustration small and the next step concrete.
scenarios.notes: A true empty account is distinct from an empty folder or filtered result. This is a proposed empty-account composition, not the captured empty-folder state.

scenarios.title: No matching items
changes: Keep the search query and active filters visible when no results match.
Offer a clear recovery action to remove filters without implying that stored vault items were deleted.
scenarios.notes: The baseline depicts an empty folder in a populated account; the optimized proposal generalizes the source no-results state without claiming a backend empty account.

scenarios.title: Loading without losing context
changes: Keep the page title and existing navigation stable while content loads.
Use calm progress feedback and prevent duplicate commands during a pending operation.
scenarios.notes: The busy state is included under page.vault in the inventory. This is an additional representative state of that page, not a new product surface.

scenarios.title: Offline and uncertain operation status
changes: Place a persistent status banner above the list with a specific explanation and contextual recovery action.
Keep cached vault contents usable where the existing service permits, and distinguish offline data from an uncertain save result.
scenarios.notes: The visible composition is offline cached-data feedback. Ambiguous creation must preserve its draft and resync-first behavior; retrying creation is not presented as safe.

scenarios.title: Verify access to a protected item
changes: Identify the protected action in the dialog title and preserve the masked background detail.
Use one password field, inline feedback, and a clear Verify action.
scenarios.notes: Master-password reprompt is retained as an access boundary. The schematic uses no real secret.

scenarios.title: Confirm permanent item deletion
changes: Name the exact target and irreversible consequence above the final action.
Keep Cancel visually safe and use error color only for the destructive confirmation.
scenarios.notes: Moving an item to trash is reversible and requires different wording from permanent deletion. Folder deletion must preserve its actual source semantics.

scenarios.title: Manage secure Sends
changes: Give text and file Sends recognizable type icons and readable expiry/access metadata.
Keep Copy link as the frequent row action and move edit/delete to a consistent overflow menu.
scenarios.notes: Sharing, access counts, expiry, and deletion remain subject to the source Send service. This review introduces no link-preview or recipient-tracking feature.

scenarios.title: Create a text Send
changes: Put the name and text content first, followed by grouped lifetime and access restrictions.
Use a single Save action and explicit labels for deletion date, expiry, and optional access password.
scenarios.notes: The composition shows content, lifetime, and selected access restrictions. Disabled state, private notes, audience details, and custom date inputs are not all depicted; implementation must retain those existing options. No share operation is performed.

scenarios.title: Create a file Send
changes: Show the selected filename and a clear file-picker action before optional sharing restrictions.
Use the same lifetime/access structure as text Send to reduce relearning.
scenarios.notes: The file picker remains Windows-owned and upload limits remain server/service dependent. This is a representative file-send form, not every restriction or date-picker state. Drag-and-drop is not claimed as implemented.

scenarios.title: Open a received Send
changes: Keep the received-link flow distinct from the account's outbound Send list.
Show link and optional access password before Open, then reveal received content or the existing Save file action.
scenarios.notes: The representative result is a text Send; file-download results and error states are not depicted. External received links require the live service and valid link key. The demo service cannot complete this flow.

scenarios.title: Generate a strong password
changes: Make the generated value the focus and keep Regenerate and Copy adjacent.
Group length and character controls below the result; place minimum counts and ambiguous-character settings in a quieter advanced group.
scenarios.notes: The displayed password is synthetic and is not intended for reuse. History remains an existing sensitive-content dialog.

scenarios.title: Generate a memorable passphrase
changes: Keep result placement and actions consistent with password generation.
Prioritize word count and separator; group capitalization and number options below.
scenarios.notes: The proposal preserves existing passphrase options and does not introduce a custom word-list service.

scenarios.title: Generate a username
changes: Make the username method explicit and show only its relevant options.
Reuse the generated-value, Regenerate, and Copy arrangement from the other generator modes.
scenarios.notes: Random words, plus-addressing, and catch-all remain the implemented methods; no third-party relay provider integration is added.

scenarios.title: Understand vault health
changes: Prioritize actionable categories with counts rather than inventing a composite security score.
Separate local weak/reused/HTTP findings from the explicit external exposed-password check.
scenarios.notes: The existing report categories and HIBP check remain unchanged. A not-yet-run exposure check must not be presented as a clean result.

scenarios.title: Review security findings
changes: Expand one finding category into a readable affected-item list with an explicit next action.
Retain checked, unchecked, and partial/error distinctions for external exposure results.
scenarios.notes: This is an additional review state included under page.reports. Counts and item names are synthetic; no exposure service was queried for this proposal.

scenarios.title: Import and export vault data
changes: Give import and export separate sections with clear purpose and file-format controls.
Place the plaintext warning directly beside the export action and give the import preview a clear position before submission.
scenarios.notes: Only the existing JSON/CSV flows are proposed. The initial view shows the preview position before a file is selected; loaded preview counts are not shown. No encrypted-export format, duplicate resolver, or import rollback is claimed.

scenarios.title: Confirm a plaintext export
changes: Explain that the exported file can expose vault contents before requesting the master password.
Keep filename selection delegated to the Windows save picker after verification.
scenarios.notes: This is the existing export-verification boundary. The artifact contains no exported vault and performs no operation.

scenarios.title: Review devices and sign-in requests
changes: Separate pending sign-in requests from the known-device list.
Make current/trusted status, last activity, and fingerprint verification readable without relying only on color.
scenarios.notes: Approve and deny retain their existing source flow. Remote device revocation is not introduced as a new capability.

scenarios.title: Confirm a device sign-in request
changes: Show the device identity and matching fingerprint immediately before approval.
Use an explicit Approve action and a clear explanation of what access is being granted.
scenarios.notes: The review data describes a synthetic request. Fingerprint matching remains a human verification step.

scenarios.title: Manage emergency access
changes: Separate contacts who can request your vault from accounts that trust you.
Present relationship status, access level, and waiting period together with only status-valid actions.
scenarios.notes: View and Takeover remain distinct. Source has no invitation-acceptance control on this page, so the proposal does not invent one.

scenarios.title: Invite an emergency contact
changes: Explain View and Takeover beside the access-level selection.
Keep the waiting period next to its consequence and show the invited email before Send invitation.
scenarios.notes: An invitation is not sent by generating this review artifact. The existing live server and relationship confirmation requirements remain.

scenarios.title: Security and vault locking
changes: Organize locking, device unlock, and account protection as separate setting groups.
Show policy or availability explanations directly under disabled settings instead of hiding the reason.
scenarios.notes: The screen reviews the security settings hierarchy. PIN, Hello, timeout, and device trust remain gated by existing policies, platform support, and persisted-session eligibility.

scenarios.title: Application and preferences
changes: Use aligned settings rows for tray behavior, theme, website icons, and browser integration.
Explain unavailable future settings and keep their status separate from usable options.
scenarios.notes: Clipboard timeout and screenshot protection are grouped under Security in this proposal. Start on login, minimize on copy, acceleration, SSH-agent settings, and language selection remain unavailable in source. Browser integration remains limited to portable builds; the proposal does not make unavailable options functional.

scenarios.title: Account and encryption settings
changes: Make the account email and server the leading identity summary.
Group profile, master password, and encryption settings together; separate account deletion with explicit consequence language.
scenarios.notes: The existing encryption dialog edits PBKDF2 iterations and does not expose a KDF-type selector. This proposal does not add Argon2 switching or migration controls.

scenarios.title: Change the master password
changes: Separate current-password verification from the new-password and confirmation pair.
Show the existing sign-out consequence before the final change action and keep validation inline.
scenarios.notes: Changing the master password requires a matching persisted session and logs out on success. This review performs no credential change.

scenarios.title: Review encryption work factor
changes: Explain the existing PBKDF2 iteration setting before the numeric input.
Keep current-password verification and the Apply action together with inline validation.
scenarios.notes: Source guard: this dialog only edits PBKDF2 iterations. Do not add a KDF-type selector, Argon2 parameters, benchmark results, or an unsupported migration path.

scenarios.title: Manage two-step protection
changes: Give each existing provider a readable status and an explicit setup/manage action.
Keep loading and errors local to provider management and require a successful load before exposing provider mutations.
scenarios.notes: The proposal is the provider overview, not completed enrollment. TOTP setup retains its secret/OTPAuth URI and code; recovery-code retrieval failure must remain a warning even after activation succeeds.

scenarios.title: Set up an authenticator
changes: Use a clear setup sequence: add the provided secret to an authenticator, then enter its code.
Keep the secret and OTPAuth URI selectable and the confirmation action below the code field.
scenarios.notes: The setup data is synthetic. Source exposes a Base32 secret and OTPAuth URI, so a scannable QR code is not claimed as implemented. Recovery code is shown only after successful activation.

scenarios.title: Manage security keys
changes: Use a compact credential list with clear names and a separate Add security key area.
Keep registration availability, operation status, and last-key deletion consequences visible at the affected action.
scenarios.notes: Management verification can use the existing master-password, email-OTP, or device-login access-code path. Registration itself remains Windows-owned.

scenarios.title: Review permanent account deletion
changes: Lead with irreversible consequences and any organization ownership impact.
Keep the existing staged confirmation: consequences, exact account email, then the applicable final credential.
scenarios.notes: The visible proposal is the first consequences step. It does not collapse the existing preflight, email, password/OTP, or uncertain-result safeguards into a one-click deletion.

scenarios.title: System and integration boundaries
changes: Keep the application request context clear before crossing into Windows or a third-party verification surface.
Preserve relying-party identity, origin, and explicit credential choice for browser passkey approval.
scenarios.notes: This is a review boundary diagram, not a redesign of Windows prompts, external Duo/SSO, or browser test harness pages. SimplePage is unreachable. The extension has no product popup, options page, or side panel.
